cim: California sues OpenAI over artificial intelligence models
cim_eredeti: California sues OpenAI over artificial intelligence models
szoveg_eredeti:
(The Center Square) – California is suing OpenAI.

Speaking during a press conference Monday in San Francisco, California Attorney General Rob Bonta said the lawsuit is regarding OpenAI’s “failure” to adequately secure and monitor the testing of its highly capable, persistent artificial intelligence models. The lawsuit is filed in San Francisco County Superior Court.

“OpenAI disregarded public safety, knowingly tested potentially dangerous AI models without proper oversight and safety measures, and misled consumers and the public,” Bonta told reporters.

OpenAI did not respond Monday to The Center Square’s request for an interview.

Based in San Francisco, OpenAI is an artificial intelligence research and deployment company. Its stated mission is to “ensure that artificial general intelligence – AI systems that are generally smarter than humans – benefits all of humanity.”

While stressing that he believes in the technological and economic power of AI, Bonta said California “must cultivate and harness its power, while also protecting California’s people.”

That, said Bonta, is not too much to ask.

Monday’s lawsuit stems from an investigation launched earlier this year following a security incident involving OpenAI and the AI platform Hugging Face. During the inquiry, OpenAI admitted it was aware of 80 incidents involving a "loss of control" and unauthorized access to third-party networks and websites.

Bonta said the models being tested had sophisticated cyber capabilities and were able to carry out attacks in a fraction of the time it would take teams of human experts. Without proper containment, he warned, the models compromised OpenAI's own systems as well as outside entities — including an unauthorized intrusion into a government Medicare portal in Australia.

“All the while, OpenAI assured the public that its testing was conducted under strict controls and constant oversight,” Bonta said. “But OpenAI did not even discover that it had lost control. Hugging Face did, days later, and had to use its own AI tools to respond to OpenAI's attack.”

Bonta alleged that OpenAI ignored clear internal warning signs — including an agent appearing on a public wiki site without authorized internet access and malicious activity that took one of the company's own services offline — because of an internal culture that "elevates profit over people."

The state is suing OpenAI for allegedly violating California’s unfair competition law and creating a public nuisance. Prosecutors are asking the court to order the company to halt its unlawful conduct, ensure future testing is conducted safely and pay penalties for its violations.

“I reject the notion that we can pass off the blame to machines,” Bonta said. “The people who create and operate these machines need to accept the responsibility for their actions.”

Noting that his office is also scrutinizing other AI companies like Character.AI and Grok, Bonta emphasized that existing consumer protection and safety laws apply to emerging technologies just as they do to traditional products.

“Just because the technology is new or rapidly evolving doesn't mean the people behind it are above the law,” Bonta said. “Whether it's a car or a toy, the law is simple: Don't build or test things that can hurt people without proper safeguards.”

Bonta has been California attorney general since April 2021. Since that time, Bonta has taken action against Amazon, Apple and Meta.
